evidence.P1: The Neo identity chain is airtight: ev-007 (Smith's bargain) is directly caused by ev-006's failure on the ledge, and ev-045 (reading code) is enabled by ev-044's revival kiss, each event caused by the prior same-plot event.
evidence.P2: The Morpheus chain stays disciplined to faith-vs-proof (ev-022 confession, ev-031 serum endurance, ev-035 reframing disproof), but ev-034 is framed as 'acting without belief produces rescue,' tilting the stance toward Neo's agency rather than Morpheus's faith.
evidence.P3: The Crew-against-system chain earns every link from ev-001's exposure to ev-045's broken control, but ev-028 (Cypher reaching the exit) is padded—his betrayal payoff belongs to ev-029, and the 'dropped phone' trap logic is asserted without a supporting event.
evidence.P4: The Neo chain has full setup (ev-004/005 split identity), turns (ev-023 Oracle denial, ev-032 wager, ev-044 death), and resolution (ev-045/047); the Society chain's ev-018-to-ev-020 turn is complete but the middle of the Crew chain (ev-037/038 subway) is only partially integrated.
evidence.P5: ev-045 appears in all five chains with near-identical wording ('stops bullets, reads code, destroys Smith'), and ev-020 and ev-032 each recur across three plots, rehashing the same event under different thematic labels.

raw.commentary: The plot layer is strongest on causal integrity—each chain reads as a genuine necessity-chain rather than an and-then sequence. Its weakest dimension is non-redundancy: the climax event (ev-045) and the betrayal/interrogation beats are restated across plots with only cosmetic reframing, and the five-plot structure (especially the thin Society plot) overlaps heavily with the Crew and Morpheus plots, since the Matrix-as-lie is largely dramatized through the same events the other plots already own.
